Do not assume the marker positions alone give every residue's color; use output examples to establish the complete mapping.

+# Translated motif branch
+
+Read this guide only when a noisy grid has a distinctive single-color motif amid zeros and another background color.
+

+2. Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros/background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation; test translations when the grid looks like noisy background plus one seed object.
+3. Allow rotations or reflections only if demonstrations support them. Check each candidate against all demonstrated changed and unchanged cells.
*** Add File: continual-arc/tile-count.md
+# Separator-tile branch
+
+Read this guide only when full-width and full-height separator lines partition the grid into equal tiles and the output dimensions match the tile layout.
+
+1. Map each tile to one output cell. Use demonstrations to identify which in-tile feature or count determines that cell; do not assume every unusual cell or a single marker is positive.
+2. For the observed pattern with color-8 separators and 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, emit 1 for a tile with at least two color-2 cells and 3 otherwise. Treat this as pattern-specific, not a rule for other tile tasks.
+3. Check the candidate output against every demonstration.
*** Add File: continual-arc/diagonal-stripes.md
+# Diagonal-stripe branch
+
+Read this guide only when sparse colored diagonal markers appear on a zero field.
+
+1. Identify the invariant for the marker lines: constant `row−column` for down-right diagonals, or `row+column` for down-left diagonals. Use zero-based row and column coordinates, and verify the sign convention against demonstrated outputs: down-right phase is indexed by `column−row`; down-left phase by `row+column`.
+2. If demonstrations show a periodic color sequence indexed by that invariant, infer the smallest plausible period that does not assign different colors to the same residue. Use output examples to establish the complete color mapping; marker positions alone may not reveal every residue.
+3. Color every cell from its phase rather than preserving only the sparse markers. Verify cells on several demonstrated lines and ensure the full candidate reproduces every demonstrated output.
*** Add File: continual-arc/edge-continuation.md
+# Edge-continuation branch
+
+Read this guide only when demonstrations show color 1 marking an absent continuation at a grid edge.
+
+1. Compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. The missing part may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions.
+2. Color only confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Select repeated copies from the demonstration evidence, not merely from rightmost zeros or suffix length.
+3. Check the candidate against every demonstration's changed and unchanged cells.
